operational_effect: Ransomware at cloud vendor Crossroads Technologies, which hosted Personal Touch's cloud-based electronic records, was notified to Personal Touch on Dec 1, 2019. The organization's own notice reports no downtime or care effect. A class-action lawsuit (Booker v. Personal Touch) alleged that the records were held inaccessible and that medical care and treatment were disrupted while the record system was offline; that disruption claim is a lawsuit allegation, flagged under adjudication rule R12, and is not corroborated by organization or contemporaneous news sources. 17 HHS breach entries totaled at least 156,409 impacted (Personal Touch Home Aides Inc. itself 1,890).
recovery_limitations: not reported
notes: Dataset date 2020-02-21 is the date HHS publicly listed the breach entries; the organization's own notice (Jan 28, 2020) dates the vendor ransomware notification to Dec 1, 2019. Vendor-vs-victim: the attacked system was Crossroads Technologies' cloud host, not Personal Touch's own network. Disruption detail comes mainly from class-action reporting (Booker v. Personal Touch), not from the org notice, which is silent on downtime - second coder should double-check services/operational coding. TRAP: a separate, larger Personal Touch ransomware attack occurred in Jan 2021 (753,107 people); do not merge. ADJUDICATION (rules R4/R12): the EHR/clinical records code is vendor-mediated - the ransomed Crossroads host held Personal Touch's cloud-based EHR, and the hosted service was itself the encrypted system; the only source for records being inaccessible and care disrupted is the class-action allegation, which is flagged as an allegation in operational_effect and is not treated as established fact.

operational_effect: Ransomware on the Ferguson Medical Group (FMG) network rendered all data, including all medical records, inaccessible; dataset article states the attack disrupted medical services and exposed patient records to unlawful access. No specific cancellations, closures or diversion were reported.
recovery_technical: Encrypted data restored from backups after the decision not to pay the ransom; many files were recovered.
recovery_limitations: Records for FMG services between September 20, 2018 and December 31, 2018, and all documentation scanned into the system, could not be restored and were permanently lost.
notes: DATE CONFLICT: dataset date 2020-11-04 is the settlement-approval article date; the attack itself occurred September 21, 2019 on Ferguson Medical Group (Sikeston, MO), which Saint Francis acquired after the attack. Sheet keeps dataset date per guide. COUNT CONFLICT: dataset/Bloomberg describe a class of over 90,000 patients and a $350,000 fund; HIPAA Journal, citing the HHS OCR portal, reports 107,054 affected. IDENTITY TRAP: this is Saint Francis Healthcare System, Cape Girardeau, MO - not Roper St. Francis (SC) or other Saint Francis systems.

services_affected: EHR/clinical records; imaging/radiology; laboratory; pharmacy; communications; billing/administrative; surgery/procedures; other (radiation oncology); other (cardiology); other (supply chain system)
operational_effect: All hospital systems were taken offline. Some procedures were shut down, computer-controlled cancer treatments could not be offered, diagnostic imaging was curtailed and PACS was down for days, and elective and outpatient services were cut back. Emergency and urgent care remained available (no diversion reported). Major downtime lasted roughly three weeks; care ran slower on paper. The hospital refused to pay the ransom and reported a detrimental financial impact, extra labor costs, and unplanned equipment replacement.
workaround: Paper records and manual downtime procedures, including runners ('sneakernet') carrying paper/spreadsheets between departments and copper-line fax machines; radiology read studies on modality consoles and burned images to CDs while PACS was down; radiation therapy was prioritized over work that could 'get by' on paper; the pharmacy workflow ran on downtime procedures (barcode scanning out, paper prescription pads), though prescriptions already filled remained available at Sky Lakes pharmacies; CalOre telecommunications donated extra bandwidth.
recovery_technical: Network completely rebuilt from tested-clean backups; clinical systems returned in prioritized sequence, with some servers back online by Nov 6, 2020 (568 servers per contemporaneous reporting); a replacement cloud-based Sectra PACS was built within days (radiologists reading studies on iPads by the first Friday, integrated RIS by Saturday); about 2,000 computers were replaced and new servers bought (contemporaneous November 2020 reporting; the IS director's later retrospective reports more than 2,500 PCs and 600 servers taken down - see notes); radiation oncology was back up on November 9, 2020, and the Epic EHR was restored on November 23, 2020 alongside a fully operational PACS/radiology system.
recovery_operations: Radiation oncology was back up on November 9, 2020. No source reports a date on which appointments, surgeries or admissions generally returned to normal.
recovery_limitations: Full organizational recovery took about seven months. Support systems (accounting, billing, email) were lower priority and took longer to restore. Elective and outpatient services were still cut back in mid-November 2020. 140 archived images (of 1.5 million) were permanently lost, all older and no longer clinically relevant. Significant unanticipated equipment and labor costs; ransom refused.
notes: DATE CONFLICT: dataset/announcement date is Oct 27, 2020, but the Washington Post reported the hospital was hit Monday morning (Oct 26) and HealthLeaders dates the initial phishing click (just after noon Oct 26) and encryption (about 11 p.m.) to Oct 26, with identification as ransomware by about 5 a.m. Oct 27; the dataset timeline lists discovery as Oct 28. Sheet keeps dataset date. COUNT CONFLICT (adjudication rule R11, contemporaneous sources govern): contemporaneous November 2020 reporting says about 2,000 computers replaced and 568 servers; the IS director's retrospective accounts say more than 2,500 PCs and 600 servers were taken down, and a Cisco case study says 650 servers; the recovery text uses the contemporaneous figures and records the retrospective ones here. PHARMACY (rule R5): pharmacy is coded because the IS director's retrospective reports barcode scanning out and prescription pads exhausted during the EHR downtime; contemporaneous reporting that prescriptions already filled remained available is a continuity fact, not an absence of pharmacy disruption. DIVERSION: emergency and urgent care remained open and fully operational per the hospital and HIPAA Journal, so emergency care/patient diversion is reported absent for Sky Lakes itself; diversion described in national Ryuk-wave coverage refers to other hospitals. Part of the coordinated Oct 2020 Ryuk wave (UNC1878/Wizard Spider).

operational_effect: Attackers deleted all patient records, appointment schedules and payment information after the owners refused to pay the $6,500 ransom; the practice permanently closed on April 30, 2019, and patients had to start over at other providers with no medical records. (The dataset's January 23, 2020 CBS Detroit item reports the same $6,500 demand, deletion of patient data and FBI investigation; see notes on the identity adjudication.)
workaround: With no way to know who was scheduled, the physicians stayed at the office for a few weeks seeing patients who showed up; staff provided referrals to other providers until the closure.
recovery_limitations: All patient files were deleted after the $6,500 ransom was not paid; no restoration from backups was reported, and patients had to start over at other providers without their records (2019 coverage; see notes).
notes: IDENTITY ADJUDICATED (adjudication rule R3): the dataset record (CBS Detroit, Jan 23, 2020, naming 'Brookside Surgery Center, Battle Creek') and the spring 2019 coverage of 'Brookside ENT and Hearing Center' in Battle Creek describe the SAME incident: the $6,500 ransom demand, deletion of all records after refusal, data deleted but not shared, and the FBI investigation match across both source sets, and no separate January 2020 Brookside incident was found. The sheet keeps the dataset date (2020-01-23) and the dataset organization name; the 2019 coverage dates the attack to early 2019, with permanent closure on April 30, 2019. Claims sourced to the 2019 coverage are kept under R3. The owners determined the incident was not a reportable HIPAA breach because the attacker did not view the records (DS Tech); no HHS OCR entry was found.

operational_effect: Ransomware disrupted access to computer systems at the hospital and all clinics in Michigan and Wisconsin and took the EHR offline, causing considerable disruption; systems were shut down to isolate the threat. Nearly all patient care services, including the 24/7 emergency department, remained open and operational - no closure or diversion was reported.
workaround: Established contingency procedures for continuous safe patient care; clinical staff shifted to manual procedures and used paper copies in place of digital records; third-party security and forensic experts were engaged to restore systems.
recovery_technical: Systems were inspected, cleaned, restored from available backups and tested one by one before being brought back online; recovery efforts were reported complete just shy of one month after the Oct 17 attack (mid-November 2020).
recovery_operations: Routine patient care was maintained throughout the recovery; no separate service-resumption milestone was reported because services had remained operational.
recovery_limitations: A November 19, 2020 update reported about 5 percent of systems still remained to recover and full system recovery was not expected until the end of the year (see notes on tension with the 'recovery complete' report). At discovery there was no indication any data was accessed or taken.
notes: Name: dataset spells the victim 'Dickingson'; the organization is Dickinson County Healthcare System (Iron Mountain, MI). Part of the same Oct 2020 Ryuk wave as Sky Lakes. RECOVERY TENSION: TechTarget (Nov 17) reported recovery 'completed' just shy of one month, while a Nov 19 local update reported ~5% of systems left and full recovery expected by year-end; both are coded, in limitations and technical respectively.

operational_effect: reported absent: MultiCare stated the breach was isolated to Woodcreek Provider Services' server, a separate system from MultiCare Health System, and that the primary electronic medical records database was not affected; Woodcreek stated the server containing its medical records system was untouched. No disruption to MultiCare care delivery was reported. The impact was data exposure: scanned clinical/financial data and business records on a vendor archive server were stolen, affecting about 210,000 people.
recovery_technical: The stolen data was returned after an undisclosed ransom was paid (by the vendor side); Woodcreek received a copy of the recovered data set on January 18, 2021.
recovery_limitations: Breach notification to about 210,000 affected individuals was still in preparation in February-March 2021 (Feb 17, 2021 letter to the Washington Attorney General); 207,000 individuals were confirmed affected via Woodcreek, with the count expected to rise.
notes: VENDOR-VS-VICTIM TRAP: the ransomware hit Netgain Technology, IT vendor to Woodcreek Provider Services, which supports MultiCare-owned pediatric/urgent-care clinics; MultiCare's own systems were not attacked. DATE VARIANCE: dataset/Becker's date the attack 'on or about Dec 2, 2020'; Woodcreek's AG letter says ransomware was deployed Dec 3, 2020, with attacker access from Nov 23/24, 2020 and possibly as early as September 2020. IDENTITY TRAP: code only the Tacoma, WA MultiCare; other MultiCare/Netgain victims (e.g., Ramsey County, MN) are separate.

operational_effect: Organization website was unreachable for the past few days
recovery_limitations: not reported
notes: Sparse single-source reporting (DataBreaches.Net only); no organization statement or care-delivery effect found; see notes_2021.md

operational_effect: not reported
recovery_limitations: Identification of affected individuals was prolonged: forensic investigation concluded 2021-10-14 and preliminary review 2021-11-08; data mining ran Dec 2021-Oct 2022 and individual notification letters began 2022-11-28
notes: Live EMR explicitly reported unaffected in 2022 AG notices, so EHR not coded; affected count conflicts: 57,730 (HHS, Jan 2022 reporting) vs 75,992 (Maine AG, Dec 2022); see notes_2021.md

operational_effect: reported absent: hospital said operations continued without interruption, patient care was not interrupted and no patients were at risk of harm
workaround: Hospital continued to operate under its emergency procedures
recovery_limitations: Investigation and data analysis continued for months: patient information involvement determined 2021-11-30 (patient letters 2021-12-30) and employee/physician involvement determined 2022-02-07 (letters 2022-03-04). The breach was reported to HHS OCR as affecting 9,880 individuals.
notes: EHR (adjudication rule R4): sources report that Vice Society gained access to the electronic medical record system and that 'the EHR was breached', with data exfiltrated before files were encrypted; no source reports clinicians losing EHR access or any specific service downtime, and the hospital stated patient care was not interrupted. Under R4, unauthorized access or exfiltration alone does not code a service, so EHR/clinical records is NOT coded; the hospital's own AG letter describes 'an incident that disrupted the operations of our IT systems', coded as general IT systems (unspecified) under rule R6. CA AG letters give access window 2021-08-21 to 2021-09-01 vs dataset incident date 2021-08-27 (the identification date). No source states when or whether the affected systems were restored.

operational_effect: not reported
recovery_technical: At the vendor: ransom was paid after consulting cybersecurity experts and the FBI, hackers returned the stolen data, and the vendor blocked further access and strengthened its security measures
recovery_limitations: not reported
notes: Vendor-vs-victim incident: attack was on the online data storage vendor, not Harvard Eye's own clinical systems; HIPAA Journal says it is not clear whether files were encrypted; dataset date 2021-01-15 is the date the vendor alerted Harvard Eye; see notes_2021.md

operational_effect: reported absent: the attack did not affect the functioning of the hospital and its current activity was not interrupted
workaround: Continuity of operations ensured through offline registers (also translated as offline backups/registries); ransom was not paid
recovery_limitations: not reported
notes: Hospital is in Bucharest, Romania, not Szczecin, Poland as briefed; sources are Romanian (SRI/CERT-RO via Agerpres) read in English translation; see notes_2021.md

operational_effect: Clinic computer system was shut down after the ransomware was detected; no cancellations, diversion or other care-delivery effect was reported
recovery_limitations: not reported
notes: Paper charts are the clinic's standing practice (explains why diagnoses were not involved), not a reported incident workaround, so not coded as workaround; see notes_2021.md

operational_effect: reported absent - organization stated Ascension networks and Coastal Cardiology's current (active) medical record system were not affected, and the legacy network was not used for current business operations; only legacy systems (pre-Oct. 5, 2021 records) were encrypted
recovery_limitations: Legacy EMR data remained encrypted and inaccessible, so the organization said it was unable to tell exactly what information was affected; breach notice to HHS submitted Oct. 14, 2022 and patients offered 2 years of credit monitoring
notes: Legacy-system-only incident: ransomware encrypted a retained legacy EMR, not the active EMR. Affected data related to visits prior to Oct. 5, 2021; 71,227 individuals per later reporting. Do not code as a clinical downtime event.

operational_effect: Patient appointments canceled or rescheduled and patient portal access suspended; databases/patient records systems taken offline; a St. Clare Hospital patient reported still waiting about two weeks for MRI results and a 3-hour wait after an X-ray
workaround: Staff at St. Anthony Hospital shifted to a makeshift paper system of record keeping and used phones to connect with other providers and insurers (per Becker's account of a patient report)
recovery_technical: By Oct. 17, 2022 VMFH was getting some of its patient records systems back online after taking databases offline; parent CommonSpirit later said systems were returned to the network once secured, with additional security and monitoring tools
recovery_limitations: Restoration was partial/phased: only some records systems back by Oct. 17; VMFH patient breach letters were not sent until Dec. 1, 2022.
notes: This row is VMFH's slice of the parent CommonSpirit Health ransomware incident (unauthorized access Sept. 16-Oct. 3, 2022; disclosed Oct. 4). Parent-level statements are used only where reporting ties them to VMFH or VMFH facilities (St. Clare, St. Anthony). Note tension: CommonSpirit said Virginia Mason Medical Center (a VMFH component) had minimal operational impact, while VMFH as a division reported cancellations - coded to VMFH division reporting. Ambulance diversion was reported for MercyOne (Iowa), NOT for VMFH, so emergency care/diversion is not coded here. ADJUDICATION (rule R9): CommonSpirit's parent-level report that as of Nov. 9 not all EHR systems and patient portals were back online does not explicitly cover VMFH, so it is recorded here as notes only and is not coded in VMFH's recovery fields.

operational_effect: More than 100 Colosseum Dental Benelux practices were forced to close for days; reporting says 120 practices in the Netherlands were shut down the prior week and the company said the attack seriously disrupted its duty of care to patients
workaround: Dental emergencies were temporarily accommodated with colleagues outside Colosseum Dental
recovery_technical: Organization negotiated with the attackers and paid a ransom (reported as over 2 million euros, unconfirmed by the company); spokesperson said it seemed the organization had got all its data back
recovery_operations: Affected practices were expected to return to normal operation during the week of Aug. 8, 2022; most of the 120 Netherlands practices were reported open again that week
recovery_limitations: Attackers had deleted backups before encrypting systems and backup servers did not hold all the data, which reporting says left no option but to pay; whether any data was leaked was uncertain at the time
notes: Identity/geography trap: despite the dataset label and task framing, all reporting found describes Colosseum Dental BENELUX (130+ branches in the Netherlands and Belgium), not a UK chain; the affected practices reported closed were in the Netherlands. Attacker named as LV ransomware. Company never publicly confirmed ransomware in its first (Aug. 7) statement - confirmation comes from later reporting and its own statement about paying/negotiating with attackers. Ransom amount (over EUR 2 million) is from Volkskrant sources via NL Times; the company declined to confirm the amount.

operational_effect: reported absent
recovery_limitations: not reported
notes: VENDOR INCIDENT (adjudication rule R1): the organization attacked was Geisinger's printing and mailing vendor, OneTouchPoint (OTP), whose systems were encrypted in April 2022 (unauthorized access from Apr. 27; encrypted files discovered Apr. 28). ransomware_confirmed = yes describes the attack event behind this record, confirmed at the vendor level; no source reports any encryption at, or disruption to, Geisinger itself. OTP's breach notice states 'Our business customers' systems were not impacted by this incident', so operational_effect is reported absent. Geisinger was one of 37 affected OTP customers (1,073,316 individuals affected across all customers per Maine AG reporting; no Geisinger-specific count or notice was found). Dataset date 2022-08-02 is the Becker's article date; OTP began notifying customers June 3, 2022, and individual letters were mailed in late July 2022. Do NOT confuse with the separate 2023/2024 Geisinger/Nuance breach, a different incident.

operational_effect: CHI Health reported IT system and EHR outages across its Omaha hospitals including Immanuel Medical Center; some patient appointments were rescheduled and some surgeries at CHI Health facilities were delayed, including a colonoscopy canceled on arrival on Oct. 3
workaround: Parent CommonSpirit stated facilities were following existing protocols for system outages (organization statement reported Oct. 5-6); no Immanuel-specific workaround was reported
recovery_technical: CHI Health announced on Oct. 18, 2022 that it was in the process of restoring electronic systems taken offline after the ransomware attack.
recovery_limitations: Breach notification was still pending at the time of early reporting.
notes: Immanuel Medical Center is CHI Health Immanuel in Omaha, a CommonSpirit facility; this is the same parent CommonSpirit ransomware incident as the VMFH row (access Sept. 16-Oct. 3, 2022). Early Oct. 5-6 reporting called it only an IT security issue / suspected ransomware; CommonSpirit confirmed ransomware on Oct. 12, and an April 2023 CommonSpirit update listed CHI Health Immanuel Omaha among 164 affected facilities. Surgery/appointment effects are reported at CHI Health level, with Immanuel named among the Omaha hospitals with EHR outages - no Immanuel-only effect figures were found. Dataset date 2022-10-06 is the Infosecurity article date; incident onset was Oct. 3. ADJUDICATION (rule R9): CommonSpirit's parent-level Nov. 10 report (the majority of impacted hospitals/clinics had EHR access again; portal appointment scheduling still being restored) does not explicitly cover Immanuel, so it is recorded here as notes only and is not coded in Immanuel's recovery fields.

operational_effect: Payroll/timekeeping (Kronos) outage affected more than 2,000 employees: about 55% were overpaid and about 45% underpaid; some HR-related systems were down for several months. No effect on patient care was reported. Organization stated no personal employee information was compromised
workaround: Multiple departments manually input data to keep paychecks going; the payroll department manually processed paychecks over five pay cycles under a contingency plan
recovery_technical: Vendor Kronos completed the first restoration phase on Jan. 22, 2022 (core time, scheduling and HR/payroll functionality) and Kronos was again fully functional in early March 2022
recovery_operations: Once access was restored Cheyenne Regional immediately began reconciling all employees' paychecks and corrected all underpayments
recovery_limitations: Overpayments were still being recovered at the Mar. 26 report: employees were given several payback options, including repayment over an extended period; the system was described as believed restored to accuracy, with employees invited to check with payroll
notes: Vendor incident: the direct victim was Kronos/UKG (Kronos Private Cloud), not Cheyenne Regional - its cyber insurance could not be used because it was a secondary victim. Date trap: dataset date 2022-03-26 is the Wyoming Tribune Eagle article date; the Kronos outage began Dec. 11, 2021, so most downtime and restoration precede the dataset date and fall in Dec. 2021-Mar. 2022. Only administrative (payroll/HR) impact is reported; no clinical service impact was reported.

services_affected: EHR/clinical records; laboratory; pharmacy; scheduling/appointments; emergency care/patient diversion; surgery/procedures
operational_effect: IT network taken offline late Thu 2023-02-02 as a precaution. EMS patients diverted (only Level 1 traumas from the immediate service area, plus stroke and heart attack patients, accepted); all non-emergency surgical and outpatient procedures canceled and rescheduled and non-emergency appointments rescheduled. Disruption continued into the next week: non-emergency surgeries and outpatient procedures were still canceled on Mon 2023-02-06 and some EMS diversion was still in place on 2023-02-08. Total IT downtime was 13 days (February 2-15, per TMH).
workaround: Existing system-downtime procedures with paper documentation (paper forms, prescription pads and handwritten notes at registration, admission and during care); EMS patient flow coordinated with HCA Florida Capital Hospital and Leon County EMS, with patients routed to HCA; labor and delivery continued as normal at the Women's Pavilion.
recovery_technical: Systems were reviewed, prioritized and brought back online one by one during the downtime; on February 15, 2023 TMH announced it had fully restored its computer systems and transitioned back to electronic medical records rather than paper documentation. (A TechTarget report of the restoration announcement was published 2023-02-23; TMH's own February 15 statement governs the date under adjudication rule R11.)
recovery_operations: Clinical practices resumed seeing patients on Mon 2023-02-06 with limited surgeries and procedures; EMS intake increased gradually from 2023-02-08 and non-emergency procedures resumed on a limited basis; on February 15, 2023 TMH returned to standard operations at all locations: EMS diversion ended, the highest levels of trauma, stroke and heart care resumed, and scheduling of non-emergency surgeries and outpatient procedures began.
recovery_limitations: TMH cautioned that hurdles and patient delays were still expected after the return to standard operations ('we'd be remiss not to expect hurdles'), and the law-enforcement investigation continued after restoration. Breach notification to 20,376 individuals (reported to HHS OCR) began 2023-03-31.
notes: CONFIRMATION (adjudication rule R2): coded yes with this caveat - TMH itself never used the word ransomware, calling it only an 'IT security issue'/'cyberattack'; the yes rests on sources with direct knowledge describing it as a suspected ransomware attack (DataBreaches/Florida Politics) and national outlets reporting an apparent ransomware attack (AP wire; Fox News), with no source contradicting it; HIPAA Journal's review of TMH's breach notice notes it is unclear if ransomware was used. TMH's notice gives an unauthorized-access window of 2023-01-26 to 2023-02-02, while 2023-02-02 is the downtime start. TMH confirmed its EMR system was not accessed by the attackers, which is distinct from clinicians losing access to records during the downtime. PHARMACY (rule R5) is coded from TMH's own downtime description (paper prescription pads replacing an electronic process). Later framing conflict (rule R11): Becker's (2023-02-28) reported TMH as saying the event 'did not impact patient care', which conflicts with contemporaneous reporting of canceled procedures and EMS diversion if read as a statement about service availability; it is recorded here and not coded. A separate Dec 2023 breach at vendor ESO Solutions also involved TMH patient data; different incident, not coded.

organization: Manchester Memorial and Rockville General Hospital
services_affected: EHR/clinical records; imaging/radiology; laboratory; scheduling/appointments; emergency care/patient diversion; surgery/procedures; communications; billing/administrative; other (wound healing center); other (urgent care center); other (women's wellness center); other (outpatient physical therapy)
operational_effect: Emergency departments at Manchester Memorial and Rockville General closed for much of Thu 2023-08-03 and patients were diverted to other nearby medical centers; the EDs reopened late Thursday. Elective surgeries, outpatient appointments and blood drives were suspended and many primary care services were closed on Fri 2023-08-04. Several outpatient services (elective surgeries, gastroenterology procedures, outpatient blood draws, outpatient physical therapy, outpatient medical imaging) and facilities (wound healing, urgent care, women's wellness) were closed until further notice. Key systems were still offline more than two weeks later, and the hospitals were unable to bill properly for about six weeks.
workaround: Downtime procedures including paper record-keeping; a temporary phone system was set up for patients to contact providers; patients whose appointments were affected were contacted individually.
recovery_technical: Prospect reported progress recovering critical systems on 2023-08-18 but no definitive restoration timeline; ECHN reported by 2023-09-19 that its computers were back online at Manchester, Rockville and Waterbury hospitals and throughout its network.
recovery_operations: Emergency departments reopened late Thu 2023-08-03; by mid-September 2023 ECHN officials said hospital operations had largely returned to normal for patients.
recovery_limitations: Billing disruption lasted about six weeks: the hospitals could not properly bill patients or pay medical supply vendors and could not receive Medicaid reimbursements (Connecticut provided $7 million in support); bill-payment problems and patient confusion persisted after systems returned.
notes: Part of a Prospect Medical Holdings-wide attack that began Thu 2023-08-03; dataset incident date 2023-08-04 is the first full day of reported disruption/article date. Prospect initially called it a data security incident, but a Prospect/Crozer spokesperson and ECHN's COO both confirmed ransomware. Rhysida later claimed responsibility (2023-08-24) per later reporting; dataset attacker field is empty. Waterbury Hospital is a sister Prospect facility in Connecticut, not part of this record's victim name; the paper-records quote in the dataset article is Waterbury-specific, so ECHN workaround coding rests on system-wide and ECHN-specific sources.

operational_effect: Internal systems stopped working on 2023-07-27 when an intrusion and data encryption were discovered (per the Lithuanian State Data Protection Inspectorate decision summarizing the hospital's breach notification). Certain radiology services could not be provided and employees' ability to perform administrative functions was limited. No emergency-department closure, diversion or cancellation reporting was found.
recovery_limitations: Individual breach notifications were still being issued in stages months later (8 people on 2023-08-21; 19 people on 2023-09-27), and the Inspectorate recorded that about 48,000 files had been published.
notes: Major date conflict: dataset date 2023-08-19 is the date DataBreaches reported the NoEscape leak-site listing; the hospital's own breach notification (per the 2025-04-04 Inspectorate decision) states the breach occurred 2023-07-27 and was reported 2023-07-28, affecting about 22,000 data subjects. Key official source is in Lithuanian and contains redactions where response details would appear, so workaround and recovery are not reported in accessible sources. Attacker claims (servers encrypted; sensitive documents) are NoEscape's own statements relayed by DataBreaches, not independently verified.

operational_effect: reported absent - Fallon had ceased operations in December 2022, months before the Feb-Apr 2023 intrusion, and the compromised system was a retained data storage archive kept to comply with legal obligations, so no active care services existed to be disrupted. The impact was a data breach: 911,757 people affected per the submission to the Maine Attorney General.
recovery_limitations: Review of the compromised files and identification of affected individuals was not completed until 2023-12-27 (the dataset incident date), when breach notifications to 911,757 people began, roughly eight months after detection.
notes: STRUCTURAL ABSENCE (adjudication rule R10): services_affected and operational_effect are coded 'reported absent' on a structural basis - the organization's own notice establishes that Fallon ceased operations in December 2022 and that the compromised system was a retained data storage archive kept to comply with legal obligations, so no active care services existed to be disrupted; no source contains an explicit 'no impact on operations' sentence. Date trap: dataset date 2023-12-27 is the investigation-conclusion/notification date, not the attack. Intrusion ran 2023-02-17 to 2023-04-22 (Massachusetts AG materials end the window 2023-04-21); detection is given as 2023-04-21 in Transformative's letter as quoted by SafetyDetectives and as 2023-04-23 by SecurityWeek. Transformative's own letter did not name the attack type; ransomware attribution rests on ALPHV/BlackCat's claim of responsibility (late April 2023) and news reporting. Breached archive was Fallon's; notification was made by parent Transformative Healthcare.

operational_effect: not reported
recovery_limitations: Breach notification was delayed about a year: the intrusion was detected 2023-06-03, the review of impacted files was not completed until 2024-05-09, and 377,911 individuals were notified starting June 2024.
notes: Identity trap: the coded victim is Eye Center of Northern Colorado, but the breached organization was its business associate/management company Panorama Eyecare; Eye Center is one of four clients named in LockBit's claim, and the claimed 798 GB covers all four clients collectively, not Eye Center alone. Date trap: dataset date 2023-07-11 is the LockBit leak-site listing; Panorama's notice gives unauthorized access 2023-05-22 to 2023-06-04, detected 2023-06-03. Panorama's own notice never mentions LockBit or ransomware and does not confirm encryption (DataBreaches noted it was unclear whether LockBit encrypted or only exfiltrated); no source reports any disruption to eye-care services. ADJUDICATION (rule R7): Panorama Eyecare's June 2024 statement that external experts were engaged and that all of its systems and networks 'are now secure' is response/securing language, not a restoration milestone (no outage was ever reported), so recovery_technical is not reported.

operational_effect: HNNCSB's own statement reports technical disruptions to certain computer systems, discovered 2023-11-12. No source found reports closures, cancellations, diversion or any other specific effect on behavioral-health service delivery.
recovery_limitations: Protected health information involvement was not confirmed until 2023-12-20, and individual notifications were mailed around 2024-01-11, roughly two months after discovery.
notes: Date conflict: dataset date 2023-11-25 is the DataBreaches article date about AlphV's leak-site listing (last-chance message 2023-11-24); HNNCSB's statement says stealth access began about 2023-09-26 and disruptions were discovered 2023-11-12. AlphV's claim of over 800 GB stolen is an attacker claim; HNNCSB confirmed PHI was involved but not the volume. HNNCSB is a behavioral-health community services board, not a hospital. Minor inconsistency: Kroll monitoring is stated as 12 months in the Montana-filed letter and 24 months in the Massachusetts-filed letter. ADJUDICATION (rule R7): HNNCSB's statement that it promptly took steps to secure its systems and engaged outside cybersecurity experts is response language, not a technical-restoration milestone, so recovery_technical is not reported; no restoration date or return-to-normal statement was found.
